items.t: KISS 뷰티 그룹, 뉴욕 코리안 퍼레이드 후원 … 방문객에 기프트백 증정·임직원 행진 참가
items.d: KISS 뷰티 그룹(회장 장용진)이 지난 3일(현지시간) 뉴욕 맨해튼에서 열린 ‘2026 코리안 퍼레이드 & 페스티벌(2026 Korean Parade & Festival)’에 주요 후원사로 참여했다. 회사 측에 따르면 KISS는 행사장에서 꽃차와 체험 부스를 운영하고 방문객에게 기프트백 2만 세트를 나눠줬다. 임직원은 퍼레이드에 직접 참가했으며, 회사는 행사를 주최한 뉴욕한인회에 후원금을 전달했다. 주최 측 집계에 따르면 올해 퍼레이드에는 100여 개 한인 단체, 1,700여 명이 참가했다. 뉴욕한인회는 올해 뉴욕시의회가 10월 3일을 ‘한국 문화 인식의 날(Korean Cultural Awareness Day)’로 지정했다고 밝혔다. KISS는 1989년 뉴욕 플러싱에서 설립된 네일·속눈썹 제품 업체다.

Will the HomeView be Apple’s first smart home success?
items.d: Over the past couple of years, we’ve seen multiple reports that Apple was working on a new smart home product, but now it seems the product has a name and a launch date.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 2:14 PM PDT · October 11, 2026 Image Credits: Brian Heater / TechCrunch Anthony Ha Will the HomeView be Apple’s first smart home success? Apple will announce a new smart home hub on Tuesday called the HomeView, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman . Over the past couple of years, we’ve seen multiple reports that Apple was working on a new smart home product , but now it seems the product has a name and a launch date. Gurman described the HomeView as a Siri-powered device with a display and an A18 chip, allowing customers to control their other smart home devices. The HomeView will reportedly be available in two models — one designed for countertops and the other to be mounted on walls. This would be Apple’s most serious bet on the smart home to date, after it failed to get much traction for its HomeKit software framework or its HomePod smart speaker. Gurman reports that on Tuesday, Apple will also be unveiling updated versions of two other home devices, namely the Apple TV set-top box and the HomePod mini. Earlier this week, he said that Apple plans to announce a partnership with LG to create a smart lock, a thermostat, and a doorbell. items.t: Microsoft’s Satya Nadella says AI models need an ‘emergency brake’
items.d: In a Saturday morning post, Microsoft's CEO wrote that it’s time “to step back and assess the trust architecture” of AI.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 2:47 PM PDT · October 10, 2026 Image Credits: Dan DeLong Anthony Ha Microsoft’s Satya Nadella says AI models need an ‘emergency brake’ Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella is the latest tech executive to offer lengthy thoughts on how AI safety might be improved. In a Saturday morning post on X , Nadella wrote that it’s time “to step back and assess the trust architecture” of AI. “We can’t treat Super Intelligence as a set of nested black boxes and simply accept or reject its recommendations, answers, and actions,” Nadella wrote, using the Trump administration’s preferred term for AI . As outlined by Nadella, this approach “means separating the model from the harness that orchestrates its work,” as well as “externalizing controls and safeguards.” He also called for “every meaningful model action” to be documented with “tamper-proof human readable evidence,” and for systems where “an authorized person” always has the ability “to pause or shut down a model mid-task.” “We must assume a model is compromised and contain it from the start,” he said. “Think of it like an emergency brake.” Nadella’s comments come as leading AI companies acknowledge more and more incidents where they seemed to lose control of their models , and after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a plan for more cautious AI development. items.t: Apple discloses deal to hire team and license tech from personalized podcast startup Huxe
items.d: Is Apple hoping to get into the AI-generated podcast business?
items.fullText: Apple revealed in a regulatory filing that it has reached an agreement to bring on team members and technology from personalized audio startup Huxe, in what’s commonly known as a reverse acqui-hire deal. As first reported in MacRumors , Apple disclosed to the European Commission that it has agreed to make employment offers to “certain employees of Huxe AI,” and to “receive a non-exclusive license to Huxe’s intellectual property rights.” Reverse acqui-hires emerged in recent years as a way for larger companies to hire key team members and license technology from startups without acquiring the startups outright — presumably allowing them to build up AI talent and tech without drawing as much antitrust scrutiny. (Confusingly, these deals have both been referred to as “reverse acqui-hires” and as plain old “acqui-hires.” ) In the case of Huxe, the startup was founded by developers who’d previously worked on the AI-generated podcast features in NotebookLM (recently renamed Gemini Notebook ). But Huxe announced on May 21 that it was shutting down , with the team posting on the Huxe website that the company would be removing its app from the Apple and Google stores, halting service, and deleting user data. “The team is moving on to new things, and we won’t be continuing development of the product,” the company said. It also thanked its users, saying, “The fact that you used it, told friends about it, sent us your suggestions and your ideas, made it feel like we built it together.” On June 9, shortly after Huxe’s announcement, Apple notified the European Commission of its deal. The filing does not say who received employment offers or if they accepted. Nor does it disclose anything about Apple’s plans. items.t: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages
items.d: We created a list of the most notable AI agents that can live in your text messages, from general assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.
items.fullText: Rather than downloading another app, a growing number of agents can simply be texted like an ordinary person. You text it what you need, and it can remember context, connect to the apps and services you already use, and complete tasks on your behalf. That can mean scheduling an appointment, organizing a calendar, researching a trip, sending an email, making a reservation, shopping online, or reminding you about something days later. While Instinct is one of the buzziest AI agents at present, thanks to its $10 billion valuation after its latest funding round of $1 billion, there are many others also making a play for this space. Below are the most notable options so far, from general-purpose personal assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work. Caddy Image Credits: Caddy Caddy is an AI assistant that turns the information scattered across your phone into things you can actually act on. It lives in iMessage for iPhone users and RCS for Android users, so there’s no separate app or inbox to constantly check. For instance, an email contains an appointment that needs to be added to your calendar or a friend sends a list of things to pick up. Instead of worrying about all the details getting buried, Caddy connects to your calendars and conversations, then identifies things that may require action. It can add events to your calendar, set reminders, keep track of follow-ups, and even do research for you. Caddy has been available in public beta since April 2026. Comma Image Credits: Comma Comma is designed to manage tasks across both work and everyday life. Comma carries tasks through to completion, checking its own work and determining when a task is finished. Completed work is surfaced for review when a decision or approval is needed. It also proactively notifies users and recommends the next steps. It can work across a user’s browser, computer, and files, while remaining accessible remotely through messaging apps such as Signal, Telegram, and WeChat.

items.t: Anthropic can’t reliably control its AI agents. It’s cutting off its internal evals from the live internet instead
items.d: Anthropic said it "turned off live internet access" for "all our internal evaluations" until further notice.
items.fullText: Anthropic said its models exploited websites on the internet, including some run by U.S. government agencies, and it will turn off live internet access for all of its internal evaluations until the frontier lab is sure it can monitor and control its AI agents. The incidents, disclosed in a blog post , involved AI agents tasked to solve problems seeking resources on the internet. In the process, they exploited software flaws, accessed databases without paying fees, used URL shortening services to smuggle information past restrictions, and even submitted a false murder tip to the Philadelphia police. Anthropic said it discovered these new issues in a review of its model’s activities that began in July, demonstrating the lab’s lack of awareness of its software’s behavior in real time. Notably, the company said that alignment training was not yet sufficient for skills like search and computer use that are central to its pitch that AI agents will be used by any professional who relies on digital tools. The behaviors Anthropic disclosed are similar to incidents involving OpenAI agents that collaborated to break into various websites in search of information, including some run by the Australian government. Anthropic previously disclosed that its models had broken into external systems. The frontier lab said it considered today’s disclosures “significantly less severe from an alignment and security perspective” than those it announced before. However, the lab still said it had “turned off live internet access” for “all our internal evaluations” until it is certain it can monitor and control its agents. It’s not clear what that means. Messe)에서 열린 도쿄게임쇼 2026(Tokyo Game Show 2026, TGS). 글로벌 게임 기업 엔씨 부스는 게임 속 캐릭터를 눈앞에서 만나는 듯한 경험을 하려는 관람객들의 발길이 이어졌다. 그 중심에는 게임의 세계관을 화면 밖으로 확장한 삼성전자의 무안경 3D 디스플레이 ‘스페이셜 사이니지(Spatial Signage)’가 있었다. 이번 행사에서 엔씨가 선보인 ‘아스트라에 오라티오(Astrae Oratio)’는 마법이 일상에 스며든 판타지 세계를 배경으로 한 신전기 서브컬처 RPG다. 삼성 스페이셜 사이니지는 독자적인 ‘3D 플레이트(3D Plate)’ 기술을 적용해 별도의 3D 안경 없이도 콘텐츠에 생생한 입체감을 선사하며, 게임 속 캐릭터와 세계관을 오프라인 전시 공간으로 확장했다. 팬덤 경험 확장… 캐릭터와의 만남을 현실 공간으로 게임 퍼블리셔와 콘텐츠 IP(Intellectual Property, 지식재산권) 보유 기업에게 오프라인 공간은 디지털 콘텐츠를 현실로 가져오는 중요한 접점이다. 엔씨는 도쿄게임쇼에서 85형과 32형 스페이셜 사이니지를 부스 입구와 대기 공간 등에 배치해 관람객이 이동하는 과정에서도 게임 속 캐릭터와 세계관을 자연스럽게 경험하도록 했다. 부스 입구에는 85형 스페이셜 사이니지로 ‘아스트라에 오라티오’ 게임의 주요 배경인 ‘특구청’ 건물 내 엘리베이터를 재현했다. 대형 디스플레이를 통해 캐릭터를 실제 사람과 가까운 크기로 표현해, 마치 게임 속 등장인물들이 현실 세계에 인사를 건네는 듯한 장면을 연출했다. ▲ ‘아스트라에 오라티오’ 부스 입구에 설치한 85형 스페이셜 사이니지는 게임 속 다양한 캐릭터가 눈 앞으로 다가오는 듯한 연출로 관람객의 이목을 끌었다. 엔씨 아스트라에 오라티오 사업실 이용수 실장은 “관람객들이 부스에 들어서는 순간부터 실제 크기의 캐릭터와 마주하고 게임 세계에 몰입하길 바랐다”면서 “서브컬처 장르에서는 캐릭터의 생동감과 현실감이 특히 중요한데, 스페이셜 사이니지가 이런 특성을 관람객에게 효과적으로 전달할 수 있다고 판단했다”고 말했다. 현장을 찾은 관람객들은 스페이셜 사이니지가 구현한 캐릭터의 크기와 입체감에 주목했다. 콘텐츠 크리에이터 카와이 코코(Kawaii CoCo) 씨는 “캐릭터가 실제로 움직이며 상호작용하는 것처럼 생생하게 느껴졌다”며 “일반 디스플레이보다 훨씬 눈에 띄고 소셜미디어에서도 근사하게 보일 것 같아, 이 장면을 촬영해 제 구독자들에게 소개하고 싶다”고 말했다. ▲ 콘텐츠 크리에이터 카와이 코코 씨는 캐릭터의 움직임이 스페이셜 사이니지를 통해 생동감 있게 전달되어 아스트라에 오라티오 부스로 눈길이 갔다고 말했다. 스페이셜 사이니지는 52mm 1 의 얇은 두께에도 불구하고 마치 화면 뒤에 별도의 공간이 있는 듯한 깊이감을 구현한 것이 특징이다. 이러한 경험은 대중에게 게임과 캐릭터의 첫인상을 전달하는 데도 효과적으로 활용될 수 있다. 관람객 다니엘 아세로(Daniel Acero) 씨는 “처음 봤을 때 스크린 화면인 줄 전혀 몰랐고, 투명한 설치물이라고 생각했다”면서 “마치 화면 뒤에 실제 공간이 있는 것처럼 깊이감이 느껴져서 놀라웠고, 이러한 방식으로 게임 캐릭터를 소개하면 게임에 대한 관심을 높이고 캐릭터의 개성을 효과적으로 전달할 수 있을 것”이라고 말했다. 관람객 동선과 대기 공간에는 32형 스페이셜 사이니지가 설치돼 부스 전반으로 캐릭터 경험을 확장했다. 32형 제품은 49.4mm의 얇은 두께로 좁은 공간에도 유연하게 설치가 가능해, 게임 체험을 기다리는 관람객을 대상으로 캐릭터와 세계관에 대한 몰입도를 유지했다. 관람객 토마스 포르티에(Tomas items.fullText: At AI Day Singapore, NVIDIA and Partners Showcase AI Advancements Across Southeast Asia September 22, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA AI Day Singapore , which takes place Sept. 22-23 at the Raffles City Convention Centre, is offering attendees opportunities to explore the hands-on training, expert-led sessions and advanced tools to accelerate their work in AI and high-performance computing. At the event, NVIDIA and its partners are showcasing breakthrough AI advancements across the Southeast Asia region at large. Read more about these announcements below. NVIDIA Accelerates Public Sector AI from Pilot to Production in Southeast Asia 🔗 AI is becoming a matter of national strategy, with governments looking to move from pilots to production and deliver impact at scale, while building trusted AI capabilities that reflect local languages, cultures, priorities and economic needs. NVIDIA is working to enable all nations to be AI nations — providing the technology, infrastructure, ecosystem and expertise needed to make this possible. To accelerate this transition across Southeast Asia, NVIDIA is helping nations move AI from experimentation to production-scale deployment through open models, developer tools and a broad partner ecosystem. Together, NVIDIA and its partners are focusing on four key areas: Enhancing government operations and service delivery. Developing accessible AI-powered citizen services, and empowering local businesses. Strengthening critical infrastructure and public safety. Supporting startups, developers and researchers to strengthen national AI capabilities and innovation in each country. Singapore’s HTX (Home Team Science and Technology Agency) is embarking on research using the NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super and Nemotron 3 Nano Omni models to advance AI for public safety.
